Round 1 (2026-09-06) minted the GB national core and left two things open: the OBR Economic and fiscal outlook, dropped as no-node-yet because obr.uk 403s to a browser-UA curl on both this session's networks, and the fiscal-transfer machinery the Scottish research then turned out to need. Both are closed here. **The OBR block is worked around, not defeated**: obr.uk still 403s every curl variant tried (plain, browser UA, full Chrome header set over HTTP/1.1, homepage and document paths), so the EFO was read from the first-party gov.uk copy on assets.publishing.service.gov.uk — the EFO's own foreword records that HM Treasury published it on gov.uk on the OBR's behalf, so this is a first-party route and not a snapshot. reports.title: Public Expenditure Statistical Analyses
reports.description: HM Treasury's annual accredited official statistics on UK government spending, bringing together recent outturn, estimates for the latest year and plans for the rest of the spending review period. It presents spending on both the budgeting framework (DEL/AME) and the Total Expenditure on Services framework, broken down by department, function, economic category and sector of government; chapters 9 and 10 carry the country and regional analysis. Outturn comes from the ONS public sector accounts and forward-year plans from the OBR's Economic and fiscal outlook.

reports.title: Country and regional analysis
reports.description: HM Treasury's annual statistical estimates allocating identifiable public sector expenditure between the four UK countries and the nine English regions. It is compiled from a data collection exercise across departments, devolved administrations, local authorities and public corporations, using a mix of actual regional spending and statistical apportionment on a 'who benefits' basis, and is presented within PESA as chapters 9 and 10.

reports.title: Country and regional public sector finances, UK
reports.description: An annual ONS release presenting public sector revenue, expenditure and net fiscal balance for each country of the UK and each region of England. It is distinct from the monthly Public sector finances bulletin: it takes the UK public sector finances as its control totals and apportions them to countries and regions using indicator datasets, HM Treasury's country and regional analysis being the main expenditure basis. It does not present debt or financial account data sub-nationally.

reports.title: Economic and fiscal outlook
reports.description: The Office for Budget Responsibility's five-year forecast for the UK economy and the public finances, presented to Parliament under section 8 of the Budget Responsibility and National Audit Act 2011. It covers the economic outlook, the fiscal outlook, the effects of announced government policy and the risks around the central forecast. What it must contain is set by the Charter for Budget Responsibility; the March 2026 edition was published on gov.uk by HM Treasury on the OBR's behalf.

reports.title: GDP quarterly national accounts, UK
reports.description: The ONS quarterly bulletin giving the third estimate of quarterly UK gross domestic product with the output, expenditure and income approaches balanced together, plus the quarterly sector accounts and real household disposable income per head. It is distinct from the annual UK National Accounts, The Blue Book, which is the point of annual reconciliation and supply-and-use balancing, and is compiled in line with ESA 2010.

reports.title: UK trade
reports.description: The ONS monthly bulletin on UK total trade in goods and services on a balance of payments basis, published about 40 days after the reference period. Trade is measured from over 30 sources, with HM Revenue and Customs the largest source for trade in goods at over 90% of its value; trade in services draws on ONS surveys including the International Trade in Services Survey and the International Passenger Survey.

reports.title: UK overseas trade in goods statistics
reports.description: HMRC's monthly accredited official statistics on UK trade in goods, giving aggregated and detailed data for over 9,500 commodities and around 200 partner countries. They are compiled on an International Merchandise Trade Statistics basis from customs declarations and, for Northern Ireland-EU movements, the Intrastat survey, and are the component ONS adjusts to produce trade in goods on a balance of payments basis.

reports.title: Budget Responsibility and National Audit Act 2011
reports.description: The Act that establishes the Office for Budget Responsibility and sets its main duty, to examine and report on the sustainability of the public finances. Section 4 requires the Office to prepare fiscal and economic forecasts on at least two occasions each financial year and, at least annually, an assessment of the fiscal mandate, an assessment of the accuracy of its previous forecasts and an analysis of fiscal sustainability. It also requires the Charter for Budget Responsibility.

reports.title: Charter for Budget Responsibility
reports.description: The Charter setting out the UK government's approach to fiscal policy and management of the public finances, including its fiscal objectives, the fiscal rules that deliver them and how the Office for Budget Responsibility operates in relation to them. It is required by the Budget Responsibility and National Audit Act 2011 as amended by the Budget Responsibility Act 2024, and is approved by Parliament; it determines what each Economic and fiscal outlook must contain.
reports.cadence_note: Revised occasionally rather than on a cadence, and approved by Parliament each time. The Autumn 2025 update changed the frequency at which the OBR assesses performance against the fiscal rules.

_dropped.why: NOT FOUND 2026-09-06. PESA 2026's sourcing sentence is 'Outturn data for these aggregates up to 2025-26 are taken from the public sector accounts compiled by the Office for National Statistics (ONS). The public sector accounts are a part of the National Accounts that are updated monthly.' The same PDF's glossary separately says 'The National Accounts is presented by the ONS in the Blue Book', but the sourcing sentence itself names the agency and a framework, not the Blue Book — PLAYBOOK-CORPUS section 7, 'naming the agency is not naming the artefact'. Reaching the Blue Book needs two sentences stitched together, which is not a citation. The C-grade PESA -> gb-ons-psf edge, minted this round, is what these documents actually support.

REFUSED 2026-09-06. HMRC's methodology report says 'Accredited official statistics are called National Statistics in the Statistics and Registration Service Act 2007.' The Act is named by title, but the sentence is definitional — it explains what the label means, not that the Act is the OTS's legal basis. Naming a statute in a glossary gloss is not a legal_basis edge; contrast sct-nrs-mid-year-population-estimates -> gb-srsa-2007 minted this round, where NRS states the designation was made in line with the Act.

NOT FOUND 2026-09-06. The GDP quality and methodology information says 'The estimates are then deflated by a variety of sources including lower-level components of the Consumer Price Index, Producer Price Index and Services Producer Price Index.' That names the INDEX, not the 'Consumer price inflation, UK' bulletin the corpus node stands for, and the sentence is about lower-level component series rather than the published release. The distinction matters here because ONS publishes the index inside a bulletin with a different title; left as a lead.

NOT FOUND 2026-09-06. The bulletin's chart footnote says 'Population figures for up to mid-2024 are based on mid-year UK population estimates published on 26 September 2025.' That names UK-level population estimates; the corpus node is 'Estimates of the population for England and Wales', a different artefact. A UK-wide population estimates node does not exist yet.

_dropped.edge: gb-hmrc-ots -> UN International Merchandise Trade Statistics (IMTS) (no node minted)
_dropped.why: LEAD 2026-09-06, and a good one. HMRC's methodology report states 'HMRC's Trade in goods statistics are compiled in line with the United Nations recommended methodological guidelines on International Merchandise Trade Statistics (IMTS)' — A-grade evidence naming the standard by title. There is no IMTS node in the corpus, and IMTS is the trade-statistics sibling of SNA 2008 and BPM6, which the corpus already carries: minting it would give every national trade release in the graph a standard to hang from.

_dropped.edge: gb-ons-crpsf -> ONS Inter-Departmental Business Register (IDBR) (no node minted)
_dropped.why: LEAD 2026-09-06. The CRPSF methodology guide states 'HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) administrative data on CT liabilities and location and employee data from the Office for National Statistics' (ONS) Inter-Departmental Business Register (IDBR) have been combined to provide percentage shares for the ITL1 regions.' A-grade evidence, but the IDBR is a register rather than a recurring publication and its node kind is a scope decision for Thomas, not a research one.

LEAD 2026-09-06. PESA 2026 states its functional classifications 'are based on the UN's Classification Of the Functions Of Government (COFOG)' and maps HM Treasury functions to UN COFOG level 2. COFOG is a different UN classification from COICOP 2018 and has no node; the corpus carries COICOP, ISIC and SEEA but not COFOG, which every government-finance release in the graph would be able to cite.

RESOLVED, but only by going around it. obr.uk still returns HTTP 403 to every curl variant tried this round — plain, browser UA, and a full Chrome header set over HTTP/1.1, on both the homepage and document paths, from both of this session's networks. The Economic and fiscal outlook was minted anyway because HM Treasury publishes the same document first-party on gov.uk on the OBR's behalf, which the EFO's own foreword records. Recorded here so the next agent reaching for an OBR document goes straight to assets.publishing.service.gov.uk rather than re-running the 403 ladder. The 2026-09-06 GB round's no-node-yet entry for this document is superseded by the node minted here.
